title: Common lower-truncation coproduct comparison for derived direct image
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $I$ be a set and $E_i$ a family in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $S\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ with maps $\iota_i:E_i\to S$ which exhibit an ambient coproduct. Write $F_q=H^q\circ Rf_*$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. For every pair of integers $a,q$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_i F_q(\tau_{\ge a}E_i)\to F_q(\tau_{\ge a}S)$ whose restriction to the $i$th summand is $F_q(\tau_{\ge a}\iota_i)$ is an isomorphism. Here $\tau_{\ge a}$ is canonical lower truncation for the standard cohomological t-structure.

source.place: Tag 08DZ, bounded-below spectral-sequence paragraph, with Tag 015J

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-derived-ambient-direct-sums] to identify the cohomology of the given ambient coproduct with the direct sum of the quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves of its summands. Express this sum as the directed colimit of finite sums: [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-direct-sum] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-affine-sections] give quasi-coherence, including the empty sum.

Exact sums commute with canonical lower truncation, by the cycle/kernel and cokernel formulas for the standard truncation of representatives; therefore the truncated cofan is a coproduct, and all its objects have common cohomological lower bound a. Apply the truncation hypercohomology spectral sequence to bounded-below representatives.

On the E2 page, the higher-direct-image presheaf theorem identifies the comparison locally with cohomology on the inverse images of affine opens. These inverse images are qcqs. Cohomology commutes with direct sums there, and module sheafification preserves colimits. Thus R^p f_* commutes with the sums of the quasi-coherent H^r of the truncated summands.

Exact sums commute with the kernels and images of the differentials, giving isomorphisms on every page. In total degree q only 0 <= p <= q-a can occur. Convergence gives finite filtrations; induction on their short exact sequences gives an abutment isomorphism. Naturality identifies it with the displayed coproduct comparison. If q<a both abutments vanish; the empty family is covered by the zero coproduct.
